mainEntity.name: Can I continue wearing my denture if it has a sharp edge?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is generally advisable to limit or avoid wearing a denture with a sharp edge until it has been assessed and adjusted by a dental professional. Continuing to wear it risks worsening any sore or ulcer that has already developed and prolonging the healing process. If you must wear it for social or functional reasons, try to minimise the time it is in contact with the affected tissue and remove it whenever possible to allow rest.

mainEntity.name: How quickly can a dentist fix a sharp denture edge?

acceptedAnswer.text: In many cases, smoothing or polishing a sharp edge on a denture is a relatively straightforward chairside procedure that can be completed within a single appointment. The time required will depend on the nature and extent of the damage. If the denture has a more significant fracture, or if the fit needs to be reassessed at the same time, your dentist will advise on the most appropriate course of action and the likely timescale involved.

mainEntity.name: How long should a mouth sore from a denture take to heal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Minor mouth ulcers caused by denture irritation will often begin to improve within a few days of removing the source of irritation — provided the denture is not worn during the healing period or the offending edge has been addressed. Most minor sores resolve within one to two weeks. If a sore has not shown clear signs of improvement after two weeks, it is important to have it assessed by a dentist, regardless of the suspected cause. For a focused explanation of warning signs, you may also find this related article useful: can a denture emergency cause mouth sores or cuts.

mainEntity.name: Could a sharp denture edge be a sign that my denture needs replacing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily, but it can sometimes indicate that the denture no longer fits as well as it once did. Changes in the underlying jaw bone structure are a natural consequence of tooth loss and can cause dentures to shift or sit in slightly different positions over time. If your denture is several years old and you are experiencing persistent discomfort or fit issues, your dentist may recommend relining — which involves resurfacing the fitting surface — or replacing the denture altogether. Suitability for any particular approach depends on individual clinical assessment.

mainEntity.name: Are there any home remedies I can use for a denture-related mouth sore?

acceptedAnswer.text: A warm salt water rinse is a commonly recommended and gentle home measure to help keep the area clean and support healing. Over-the-counter topical gels designed for mouth ulcers may also provide some temporary relief from discomfort. However, these are supportive measures only and do not address the underlying cause. Professional assessment and adjustment of the denture is the appropriate long-term solution, and it is important not to delay seeking care if symptoms persist or worsen.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to use a denture repair kit from a pharmacy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pharmacy-based denture repair kits are intended for very minor, temporary situations and are not a replacement for professional dental repair. Using such kits incorrectly can alter the fit of the denture, introduce materials that are not suitable for long-term intraoral use, or mask a more significant structural issue. If your denture is chipped or cracked, arranging a professional repair through your dental practice is strongly recommended to ensure both the safety and the longevity of the appliance.
